chapter: Willie Lynch, the Blue Rhythm Band and Teddy Hill
title: Lynch band personnel, Jabbo Smith and Holmes as straw boss
summary: Holmes recalls a six-to-eight piece band with Joe Steele on piano and Jabbo Smith on trumpet, and that he called the numbers.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Now, do you think that Cass McCord was in that band because Cass and Lynch were good friends?
Possibly. Very possibly, yeah. It could have been him, but it didn't have to be. Because there was
Holmes (10/11) - 3

an abundance of musicians around. And they all worked here, there, wherever you could find anything to do. And the strange thing in them days, it seemed to be... Well, maybe it's beside of the work. There seemed to be plenty of work. Maybe there weren't as many musicians.
Can you recall how big the band was?
No...well, there was about six or eight pieces. There wasn't over eight pieces, I don't think.
And Joe Steele was the pianist.
Joe Steele was the pianist...
And Willie Lynch the drummer
You alto.
Were there two or one trumpets?
That I don't remember. I know Jabbo was... No, I think it was one trumpet.
And that trumpet was...
Jabbo.
He left, and then you got Jabbo Smith.
Yeah. Whoever the trumpet was. Or maybe there wasn't another trumpet. Maybe we opened up with Jabbo in the band.
But you remember Jabbo in the band.
Jabbo was there, yeah. Definitely. Maybe he couldn't get the trumpet that he wanted, and he sent for
Holmes (10/11) - 4
Jabbo.
Well, Jabbo must have been playing very well at that time.
Jabbo was playing very well. He was about the best you could get -- I mean, at that time. Oh yeah, he was a big asset to the band. Definitely
Do you remember if he sang then? Was he singing, too?
I don't remember him singing.
And you were appointed the straw boss?

Well, it was just one of them things. Nobody appoints them jobs. Who wants them? It's just the idea that I knew a little bit more about calling the numbers and things than Willie did. So I called the numbers, what we were going to play, and different little ideas and things, you know.
Do you remember any of the numbers that you did play?
No. All of them sound alike to me.
You can't remember any single number at all?
No, not one.
Even though you called them.
Yeah. But that don't mean nothin'.
